questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi labelled which repressive British legislation as the 'Black Act' and called for an All-India mass protest against it in 1919?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rowlatt Act**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Rowlatt Act, officially known as the Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act of 1919, was passed by the British colonial government to suppress nationalist activities.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi labeled the Rowlatt Act as the 'Black Act' due to its oppressive nature and disregard for civil liberties.
 
• The act allowed the British government to arrest and detain individuals without trial and search premises without warrants, leading to widespread public outrage.
 
• In response to the Rowlatt Act, Gandhi organized the All-India Hartal on April 6, 1919, marking one of the first mass protests against British rule.
 
• The act was a major factor behind the Jallianwala Bagh massacre in Amritsar on April 13, 1919, where peaceful protestors were brutally killed, further intensifying the freedom movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vernacular Press Act:**

 
 
• Enacted in 1878 by Lord Lytton to control the vernacular press and curb criticism of British policies.
 
• Allowed the colonial government to confiscate press materials that were deemed seditious.
 
• Faced widespread opposition and was later repealed in 1882 by Lord Ripon.
 
 
 
• **Indian Councils Act:**
 
 
• Passed in 1861, 1892, and 1909 to expand Indian participation in legislative councils.
 
• The 1909 Act, also known as the Morley-Minto reforms, introduced separate electorates for Muslims.
 
• These acts were significant milestones in the evolution of legislative governance in colonial India.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution automatically suspends the Fundamental Rights during emergencies?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 358**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Article 358 of the Indian Constitution provides for the automatic suspension of Fundamental Rights under Article 19 during a National Emergency.
 
• It applies only when the emergency is proclaimed due to war or external aggression (not in cases of internal disturbance).
 
• During such emergencies, legislative and executive actions violating Article 19 cannot be challenged in a court of law.
 
• Article 358 ceases to operate once the Emergency ends, and Article 19 is automatically restored.
 
• Only rights under Article 19 are affected; other Fundamental Rights remain enforceable unless specifically suspended under Article 359.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 359:**

 
 
• Allows the President to suspend the right to move courts for enforcement of Fundamental Rights (except Articles 20 and 21) during a National Emergency.
 
• Unlike Article 358, Article 359 requires a specific presidential order for suspension.
 
 
 
• **Article 352:**
 
 
• Deals with the proclamation of National Emergency in case of war, external aggression, or armed rebellion.
 
• It forms the constitutional basis for invoking Articles 358 and 359 during emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights:**
 
 
• These are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution, guaranteeing essential rights to Indian citizens.
 
• Key rights include the Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right to Constitutional Remedies, etc.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The suspension of Fundamental Rights under Articles 358 and 359 was notably applied during the Emergency of 1975-77.
 
• The Emergency was declared under Article 352 due to "internal disturbance," later amended to "armed rebellion" by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978.

questions.question: Who among the following Sultans of Delhi started the system of Sijda and Paibos?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ghiyas ud din Balban.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• ** The correct answer is option 3, i.e. Ghiyas ud din Balban, who was the ninth Sultan of Delhi and ruled from 1266 to 1287 AD.**
 
• ** Sijda and Paibos were two forms of obeisance** that were introduced by Balban to establish his authority and enhance the status of the Sultanate in the eyes of the people.
 
• Sijda involved prostratin**g oneself before the Sultan** and touching his feet as a sign of submission and respect. P**aibos, on the other hand, required the person to kneel before the Sultan and kiss his feet.**
 
• Balban's strict enforcement of these customs was meant to reinforce the idea of the** Sultan as a divine ruler **and to discourage any challenges to his authority.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ** Muhammad Bin Tughlug, the second Sultan of the Tughlaq dynasty**, was known for his eccentricities and mismanagement of the empire.
 
• Nasir u din Muhammad was the third Sultan of the Khilji dynasty and is known for his patronage of scholars and poets.
 
• **Qutb ud-Din Aibak was the founder of the Slave dynasty and the first Muslim ruler of Delhi**.
 
• He is known for his military conquests and his construction of the Qutub Minar.

questions.question: Who among the following is related with 'Labour Theory of Property'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**John Locke.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Labour Theory of Property was given by** John Locke**.
 
• It states that property comes about by exertion of labour upon natural resources.
 
• According to Locke, when a person works on a field, that labour enters into the object thus, the object becomes the property of the person.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Adam Smith: **

 
 
• **​**In 1759 Smith published his first work, **The Theory of Moral Sentiments.** Didactic, exhortative, and analytic by turns, it lays the psychological foundation on which The Wealth of Nations was later to be built.
 
• In it, Smith described the principles of** “human nature,”** which, together with Hume and the other leading philosophers of his time, he took as a universal and unchanging datum from which social institutions, as well as social behaviour, could be deduced.
 
 
 
• **J.S. Mill: **
 
 
• **​**The ethical theory of John Stuart Mill (1806-1873) is most extensively articulated in his classical text Utilitarianism (1861).
 
• Its goal is to justify the utilitarian principle as the foundation of morals. 
 
 
 
• **J. J. Rousseau:**
 
 
• **​**As a believer in the plasticity of human nature, Rousseau holds that good laws make for good citizens.
 
• However, he also believes both that good laws can only be willed by good citizens and that, in order to be legitimate, they must be agreed upon by the assembly.

questions.question: Which of the following Institutions estimate the national income of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is National Statistical Office

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The national income in India is calculated by the** ****National Statistical Office.**
 
• The NSO was formed by merging the CSO and the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) to streamline statistical activities in India. 
 
• The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) provides the administrative and policy framework for the CSO/NSO. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **According to Simon Kuznets, National Income can be calculated by three methods.**

 
 
• **Product Method- **
 
• In this method, the net value of final goods and services produced in a country during a year is obtained, which is called the final product.
 
• **Income Method-**
 
• In this method, a total of net income earned by working people in different sectors and commercial enterprises is obtained. By this method, NI is obtained by adding receipts as total rent, total wages, total interest, and total profit.
 
• **Consumption Method-**
 
• It is also called the expenditure method.
 
• Income is either spent on consumption or saving. Hence, National Income is the addition of total consumption and total saving.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The government has decided to merge the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) with the Central Statistics Office (CSO)** under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI).
 
• The order dated 23rd May 2019 has cleared the formation of an overarching body - the National Statistical Office (NSO) through the merger of the NSSO and the CSO.

questions.question: Under Article 103 of the Constitution of India, the President shall obtain the opinion of which of the following authority before giving any decision on any question regarding the disqualification of the members of the Lok Sabha?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Election Commission**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 103** of the Constitution of India- Decision on questions as to disqualifications of members

 
 
• If any question arises as to whether a member of either House of Parliament has become subject to any of the disqualifications mentioned in clause (1) of Article 102, the question shall be referred for the decision of the President and his decision shall be final.
 
• Before giving any decision on any such question, the President shall obtain the opinion of the **Election Commission**__ and shall act according to such opinion.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Election Commission of India:**

 
 
• Formed: 25 January 1950.
 
• Objective: Election to the offices of President, Vice President, Parliament, Legislative Assemblies and Councils.
 
• Removal of Chief Election Commissioner – By a resolution passed by parliament (the two-third majority in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha).
 
• Removal of Election Commissioner – By President of India on the recommendation of Chief Election Commissioner.
 
• Article 324 – Article 329: Related to the Election Commission of India.

questions.question: The nitrogen in the ecosystem is circulated by:-
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Bacteria**__.

__
 
• The process of conversion of nitrogen (N₂) to ammonia is termed as **nitrogen fixation**.
 
• **Bacteria play a great role in nitrogen fixation**__.
 
• Nitrogen-fixing bacteria inhabit legume root nodules.
 
• Nitrogenase is the enzyme in nitrogen-fixing bacteria that catalyzes the conversion of atmospheric nitrogen into ammonia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Ammonia is first oxidised to nitrite by the bacteria Nitrosomonas or Nitrococcus.
 
• The nitrite is further oxidised to nitrate with the help of the **bacterium Nitrobacter**.
 
• These nitrifying bacteria are chemoautotrophs.
 
• The nitrate thus formed is absorbed by plants and is transported to the leaves.
 
• In leaves, it is reduced to form ammonia that finally forms the amine group of amino acids.
 
• Nitrate present in the soil is also reduced to nitrogen by the process of denitrification. Denitrification is carried by bacteria Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus.

questions.question: India’s North Central Railway Zone’s Headquarter is located in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prayagraj**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The headquarters of the North Central Railway Zone is located in **Prayagraj, Uttar Pradesh.**
 
• It is one of the 18 railway zones in India, established on **1st April 2003.**
 
• The North Central Railway Zone covers major states including **Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Rajasthan, and Haryana.**
 
• This zone is known as the **"Workhorse of Indian Railways"** due to its significant role in freight and passenger movement.
 
• The zone operates through three divisions: **Prayagraj, Jhansi, and Agra.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Railway Zones in India**

 
 
• Indian Railways is divided into **18 zones**, each headed by a General Manager.
 
• The zones are further subdivided into divisions, each managed by Divisional Railway Managers.
 
• Zones are categorized based on geographical coverage and operational efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Prayagraj**
 
 
• Prayagraj, formerly known as Allahabad, is historically and culturally significant in India.
 
• It is a major hub for railways, with important routes connecting northern and central India.
 
• The city hosts the **Kumbh Mela**, one of the largest religious gatherings in the world.
 
 
 
• **North Central Railway Zone Infrastructure**
 
 
• The zone is critical for freight operations, especially coal transportation from Madhya Pradesh.
 
• It handles key passenger routes, including **Delhi-Mumbai and Delhi-Howrah corridors.**
 
• It is equipped with modern infrastructure like **automatic signaling systems.**
 
 
 
• **Other Railway Zones**
 
 
• Some other major railway zones include Northern Railway Zone (New Delhi), Western Railway Zone (Mumbai), and Southern Railway Zone (Chennai).
 
• Each zone plays a unique role in ensuring connectivity and efficient transportation across India.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers is also known as Yarlung Tsangpo in the Tibet region of China?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmaputra**__.

__
 
• **Brahmaputra river is also known as the Yarlung Tsangpo in the Tibet region of China**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• The** Yarlung Tsangpo River** is the **longest river in the Tibet** Region, China.
 
• Downstream from Arunachal Pradesh, the river becomes wider and after reaching Assam, the river is known as the **Brahmaputra**.
 
• The river is called the Everest of Rivers because of its extreme conditions.
 
• It is also called the **Dihang **River in** Arunachal Pradesh**.
 
• It **originates **from the **Manasarovar Lake** region, near Mount Kailash.
 
• It flows southwest through the Assam Valley as the Brahmaputra and south through Bangladesh as the Jamuna.
 
• It** merges with the Ganges**, popularly known as the Padma in Bangladesh, becomes the Meghna, and ultimately empties into the Bay of Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indus:**​

 
 
• The Indus originates from the Bokhar Chu (glacier) on the northern slopes of Mt. Kailash.
 
• Jhelum, Chenab, Ravi, Beas, and Satluj are its main tributaries.
 
• The River passes by the Nanga-Parvat and turns southwest to enter Pakistan.
 
 
 
• **Sutlej:**​
 
 
• Sutlej originates from Rakshastal Lake.
 
• Rakshastal Lake is located near Lake Manasarovar and Mount Kailash.
 
• Sutlej River is also known as Shatadru (Ancient name).
 
• River Sutlej is one of the major tributaries of Indus.
 
 
 
• **Teesta:**
 
 
• ​Teesta River originates from the Pahunri (or Teesta Kangse) glacier in Sikkim.
 
• It is a tributary of the Brahmaputra.
 
• It flows through Sikkim and West Bengal through Bangladesh and enters the Bay of Bengal.
 
 

89:T

questions.question: The reservation of seats for women in Panchayati Raj institutions is provided by which of the following Constitutional amendments?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**73rd Amendment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, passed in 1992, introduced provisions for **the establishment of Panchayati Raj institutions** in India.
 
• It mandated the **reservation of one-third of seats** for women, including the position of chairpersons, in Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• This amendment added **Part IX** to the Constitution, titled "The Panchayats," and a new Schedule, **Schedule XI**, enumerating 29 subjects under the Panchayati Raj's jurisdiction.
 
• The amendment aimed at empowering women and ensuring their active participation in local self-governance.
 
• The reservation for women was designed to enhance **political representation and decision-making** capabilities for women in rural governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Part IX of the Constitution:**

 
 
• Part IX was introduced through the 73rd Amendment, focusing on rural self-governance through Panchayati Raj institutions.
 
• The Gram Sabha serves as the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system.
 
• It stipulates a three-tier structure: Gram Panchayat at the village level, Panchayat Samiti at the block level, and Zila Parishad at the district level.
 
 
 
• **Reservation for Women in Local Governance:**
 
 
• The provision for reservation of seats for women in Panchayati Raj institutions aims to **enhance women's representation in politics.**
 
• One-third of the total seats, including the positions of chairpersons, are reserved for women across all levels.
 
• This reservation is applicable to Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes as well.
 
 
 
• **Schedule XI:**
 
 
• It lists 29 functional items that Panchayati Raj institutions are responsible for, such as agriculture, education, health, sanitation, and rural development.
 
• These subjects enable decentralized governance and decision-making at the local level.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the 73rd Amendment:**
 
 
• It strengthened grassroots democracy and decentralized governance.
 
• The amendment empowered marginalized groups, including women, Scheduled Castes, and Scheduled Tribes, to participate in governance.
 
• This institutionalized local self-government, making it a constitutional mandate.

questions.question:
What does "Satyameva Jayate" mean?

A. "Truth alone triumphs"

B. "True Faith is Rare"

C. "Truth is Drivine"

D. "Truth is a Treasure"
questions.solution:
Option **3** is correct.

__
 
• "**Satyameva Jayate**" means "**Truth alone triumphs**__". 
 
• It is a part of a mantra from **Mundaka Upanishad** which is an ancient Hindu scripture.
 
• This phrase was adopted as the national motto of India on 26 January 1950 following the independence of India.
 
• This phrase is written in the Devanagari script at the base of the Lion Capital of Ashoka.
 
• Please note that this phrase along with Indian national emblem is inscribed on one side of all Indian currencies.
 
• Pandit Madan Mohan Malaviya is accredited to popularise this slogan.

questions.question: The Champaran Satyagraha of 1917, Gandhi’s first major involvement in India’s freedom struggle, was launched in support of which group?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indigo farmers in Bihar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Champaran Satyagraha of 1917** marked Mahatma Gandhi’s first major involvement in India’s freedom struggle.
 
• It was launched in support of **Indigo farmers in Bihar**, who were oppressed under the exploitative tinkathia system.
 
• The farmers were forced to grow indigo on a portion of their land and sell it at fixed prices, leading to severe financial hardship.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi’s intervention in Champaran was aimed at addressing the farmers' grievances and demonstrating the power of nonviolent resistance.
 
• The success of the Champaran movement brought attention to the plight of farmers and strengthened Gandhi’s leadership in the national movement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tinkathia System:**

 
 
• Under this system, farmers were forced to cultivate indigo on 3/20th of their land, regardless of their own preferences.
 
• The system was exploitative and caused significant economic distress for the farmers.
 
 
 
• **Role of Gandhi:**
 
 
• Mahatma Gandhi visited Champaran in 1917 after being requested by local leaders like Raj Kumar Shukla.
 
• He adopted the method of Satyagraha (nonviolent resistance) to address the injustice faced by farmers.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Champaran Movement:**
 
 
• The movement led to the abolition of the tinkathia system and improved the condition of farmers in the region.
 
• It demonstrated the effectiveness of nonviolent resistance and became a precursor to future freedom struggles under Gandhi’s leadership.
 
 
 
• **Indigo Cultivation:**
 
 
• Indigo was a dye plant that was in high demand in Europe during colonial times.
 
• The forced cultivation of indigo caused soil depletion, which further impacted farmers’ livelihoods.

questions.question: The Attorney-General for India is appointed under which Article of the Constitution of India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Article 76__.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Attorney-General of India**

 
 
• In India Attorney-General (AG) is the **chief legal advisor of the Indian government's.**
 
• The **President of India appoints **the AG on the advice of Union Cabinet under **Article 76 **of the** Constitution of India, 1950.**
 
• **The Attorney-General have an advisory role to counsel the government of India in the legal matters and their positions are hold as per the President's pleasure. **This indicates that there is no specific tenure, and that they serve until the President appoints their removal. 
 
• In addition to serving as the government's primary legal counsel, the AG of India should also appears in the Supreme Court on behalf of the government.
 
• In India, there have been **16 AGs **since 1950.** R Venkatramaniis the current attorney general** of India. In 2023, President Draupadi Murmu appointed him.. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

 
• The Attorney-General of India is also a **first law officer of the country**.
 
• **Motilal Chimanlal Setalvad** was appointed as the first attorney-general of India. His tenure as attorney general from **1950 to 1963** is still the longest tenure served by any attorney-general.
 
• The AGs has the** right of audience** to appear in **all Indian Court's **and to take part in the Parliamentary sessions, **but not to vote**.
 
• The Attorney General of India lacks executive authority, in contrast to the** Attorney General of the United States**. The Law Minister of India is the in charge of certain duties.
